sections_changed: 6. The fixed-depth reduction to density-one certificates
changes_since_the_proof_audit_edition.summary: The A076227 attribution. Section 1 gains two paragraphs stating that the word counts used here are Collatz word counts -- the shortcut Collatz map moves log x by -log 2 or +log(3/2) and the Juggler map moves log log n by the same two steps, so a word contracts in one problem exactly when it contracts in the other -- naming A076227 for the survivor counts, A100982 for the minimal certificates and A020914 for their admissible lengths, disclaiming priority for all three, and locating the contribution where the two problems part: Terras's bijection makes the fair-share densities free for Collatz, while for the Juggler map they are Hypothesis FD. Lemma 5.1 is labelled as verifying the first terms of A100982 rather than establishing them. Remark 6.2 notes that the decay it proves is a statement about Collatz residue classes as well. The Section 8 evidence table gains a row for the shared word counts. References 5 to 7 are the three OEIS entries. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed; Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are untouched. THE PSI SCOPE QUESTION, settled in this edition. Section 6 previously said that whether Winkler's normalized oscillations for A100982 determine this paper's psi was a question about the identity M_d = 2 N_(d-1) - N_d and had not been checked. Section 7 of that preprint has now been read. Corollary 11 gives only a root limit with no rate, and Corollary 12 proves that r a_3(r) divided by its lower cycle bound has liminf 1 and limsup alpha/(alpha-1) = 2.7095112914 for alpha = log2 3, the lower value attained exactly on the record minima of frac(r alpha) and the sup approached along the record maxima. That is an exact statement about the extremes of two sparse sets of orders and not an asymptotic for a general r, so it carries no error term and does not transmit through the tail. The envelope is a factor 2.71 wide while the whole oscillation of psi spans 1.06, some twenty-eight times narrower. Section 6 therefore claims psi and cites Winkler for the bound, where it previously withheld the claim. Reference 13 records both corollaries. Both were verified against this paper's own counts in tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_winkler_envelope.py. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed; Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 are untouched. THE DROPPING-TIME NAME, added in this edition. Section 1 already credited A076227, A100982 and A020914 and disclaimed priority, but described A020914 by its construction, 'the binary lengths of the powers of three'. The Collatz literature indexes it by what it means: A020914 is the set of allowable DROPPING TIMES of the shortcut map, recorded as such in its OEIS entry since 22 October 2009, with the dropping time of an individual start tabulated as A126241. The length of a minimal certificate is a dropping time. Verified in the laboratory before the sentence was written, three ways in exact integer arithmetic: the lengths carrying a minimal certificate are A020914 over d <= 21; every n in [3, 20000) has its parity word to its dropping time a minimal certificate, zero failures; every dropping time attained below 2e6 lies in A020914, no exception. Nothing mathematical changes and no claim is withdrawn. A referee was being told the construction rather than the name, and the name is the one the field indexes on. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed. VOCABULARY COLLISION DECLARED, same day, after a peer followed the cross-references. The attribution sentence said A076227 counts the residue classes on which the Collatz STOPPING time is not constant. In OEIS vocabulary that is the wrong quantity: A076227's own comment names A074473, titled 'Dropping time for the 3x+1 problem', while OEIS reserves stopping time for the steps needed to reach 1 (A006666 counts the halving steps). The paper is not simply wrong -- Terras, whom it follows, calls the first fall below the start the stopping time -- but it had declared neither convention, and after the dropping-time addition earlier today it used both in one paragraph. Section 1 now uses the OEIS term in the attribution, since that is what is being attributed, and adds a sentence naming both conventions and saying they are one object. The keyword list follows. No theorem, constant, exponent or proof changed. 2026-09-20 REVISION, ONE PARAGRAPH AND ONE REFERENCE: the exponential rate is attributed to Lagarias, Theorem D of reference [14], which the previous edition did not cite at all. That edition said the rate 'is not folklore' and credited Hikawa [9, Section 6], repeating his remark that it appears to be new for these sequences. The rate is Theorem D's eta and has been in print since 1985; the link is an identity, 2^(-eta) = 2^(H(p)-1) = p^(-p)(1-p)^(p-1)/2 = vartheta(p), verified to fifty digits. Hikawa Section 6 is now described as an independent proof in the weight basis whose constants are eta rescaled, and his novelty remark is marked incorrect. What is still his is the weight-basis form and Conjecture 7.1; nothing else in the manuscript changed, and the page count is unchanged at 41. THE VERSION STAMP AND THE RENDERED PDF HAVE NOT BEEN REVIEWED BY THE AUTHOR.
